I've been developing a project to create a video documentary series that showcases the creation of a home and lifestyle based entirely on open source technology and owner-fabrication. Housing, furnishings, workshop, microfarm, power and utilities, even personal transportation and domestic robots would--as much as possible--all be owner-built using digital fabrication tools and open source designs.

This wouldn't be a competitive reality show. More of a documentary, though it could have different teams pursuing different general designs in different locations, sort of the way shows like Amazing Spaces and their spin-offs work. And much like the approach in the old This Old House series, the different stages and features of the main build would be used as lead-ins to 'side trips' exploring more concepts and details of emerging Post-Industrial culture and technology. Visits to the different fab labs, makerspace, hackerspaces, design labs like N55, robotics and other tech labs around the world. Visits to the Swiss cooperatives, Danish cohousing communities, the various Tiny House villages, and so on. Visits to events like Maker Faires, the Solar Decathlon, Burning Man. Interviews with people like Neil Gerschenfeld, Vinay Gupta, Adam Savage, Michel Bauwens, Bruce Sterling, etc.

The point of the documentary is to use this construction project as a vehicle to give people a glimpse of a Post-Industrial lifestyle of the near future, where we can leverage these new independent production tools on greater personal freedom, mobility, and economic independence.
